correctness.rationale: The backward Poisson equations and transmission boundary conditions follow from infinitesimal generator/renewal; a geometric no-tumble block bound proves absorption and finite mean. Solving D’=-2, S’=2zD has denominator H=(p+q-pq)z+pq>0. Uniform averaging yields the rational expression; differentiation yields the strict convexity/linear symmetric case and the exact threshold including equality and λ=0. Exact symbolic algebra verified identities and an independently constructed killed finite-volume Markov generator agreed with the formula for 8 parameter sets at 3 resolutions; no finite test is treated as proof.

value.rationale: A directionally selective point detector on a closed transport track is a natural nonequilibrium search design. Contrary to the usual ballistic preference for a symmetric target, the theorem identifies the precise asymmetry condition for stochastic reorientations to improve capture, gives a unique global tuning rule independent of length and speed after nondimensionalization, and quantifies an exact 36% improvement in a canonical example. This is a structural sharp phase boundary, not a sampled parameter increment.
